name: Copper Age
description: Build a real mechanical workshop: metalworking, continuous power, control, logistics and improved ore processing.

pages.text: $(bold)Welcome to the Copper Age$()$(br2)Your first Copper Ingot ends the Stone Age. Copper is where Magneticraft2 stops being only primitive survival and starts becoming a mechanical technology mod.$(br2)You will manufacture parts, build rotational power networks, automate item movement and improve ore yield.

$(bold)1. Work the metal$()$(br2)Start with the Primitive Anvil. Turn Copper Ingots into Copper Plates, then use those plates to reinforce the first proper control and transmission components.$(br2)See $(l:magneticraft2:copper_processing)Copper Processing$() for the anvil, Mechanical Grinder and the first 2x copper-yield loop.

$(bold)2. Build a drivetrain$()$(br2)Wooden Shafts and gears teach the core Gear V2 rules. The handled gear provides manual power; Water Wheels provide continuous power; Pulleys and Leather Drive Belts carry rotation across open space; Gearboxes turn and route the network.$(br2)See $(l:magneticraft2:copper_power)Mechanical Power$().

$(bold)3. Control and protect it$()$(br2)Once the workshop grows, power must be controllable. The Clutch gives manual/redstone disconnects, the Overload Disconnect protects the source side automatically, and the Mechanical Brake deliberately applies a heavy load without breaking the drivetrain.$(br2)All three are documented in $(l:magneticraft2:copper_power)Mechanical Power$().

$(bold)4. Move items$()$(br2)Conveyor Rollers and Item Belts form the first physical logistics system. Runs can be horizontal or exactly 45 degrees, and powered belts hand stacks smoothly from one section to another.$(br2)See $(l:magneticraft2:copper_logistics)Item Logistics$() for placement rules and belt limits.

$(bold)5. Convert motion$()$(br2)The Wooden Crank turns rotational motion into a real reciprocating stroke. This is the bridge from simple rotating machinery to mechanisms such as the upcoming mechanical Bellows.$(br2)The crank's placement and linear output are documented in $(l:magneticraft2:copper_power)Mechanical Power$().

$(bold)Current Copper workshop$()$(br2)Available now: Primitive Anvil, Wooden Shafts, 8/16-tooth gears, handled gear, Small/Large Water Wheels, Small/Large Pulleys, Leather Drive Belts, Right-Angle Gearbox, Custom Gearbox, Clutch, Overload Disconnect, Mechanical Brake, Wooden Crank, Conveyor Rollers, Item Belts and the Mechanical Grinder.

$(bold)Next milestones$()$(br2)The next planned mechanisms are the Mechanical Bellows and Flywheel. Bellows will be the first major consumer of the crank's reciprocating output; the Flywheel will add rotational inertia/buffering instead of being another magic power source.$(br2)After that, Copper Age can push deeper into ore processing and the road to Tin and Bronze.

$(bold)The road to Bronze$()$(br2)Cassiterite and Tin remain the final Copper Age metallurgy goal. Tin processing should depend on the mechanical infrastructure learned here.$(br2)Producing the first Bronze will mark the transition into the Bronze Age.
